bounded_audit.status: source-equation/algebraic scope audit plus numerical sanity check; not S8/S11/S12 reproduction
bounded_audit.printed_final_model: The final paper's rotational drift is Q(t+dt)=Q(t)R(dtheta), where Q is the N-by-k orthonormal manifold basis and R is an orthogonal k-by-k coordinate rotation. Therefore P(t)=Q(t)Q(t)^T is exactly invariant under the printed drift. This can change within-span coordinates and, if W is rebuilt from Q and W_k, within-span recurrent dynamics, but it does not rotate the structural manifold into new ambient dimensions.
bounded_audit.principal_angle_implication: Methods Eqs 35-37 define principal angles from the singular values of the cross-product of k-dimensional empirical activity bases. If constrained activity remains full-rank inside the invariant span(Q), a pure right rotation cannot by itself create nonzero k-dimensional subspace angles. A high S11 angle therefore requires additional semantics such as empirical rank loss/weak modes, off-span activity/noise, a different code-level rotation, different rank/operands, or another implementation detail.
bounded_audit.scope_conclusion: The final S8/S11/S12 rotation suite does not directly instantiate the ambient-subspace rotation requested in the peer review under the printed Eq.34. It tests a within-manifold coordinate/dynamics remapping and any induced empirical covariance drift. Therefore evidence from these panels should not be generalized to tracking a genuinely rotating ambient neural manifold until code semantics or an explicit ambient-rotation control establish that regime.

candidate_update.positive_scope: adaptive empirical-subspace tracking remains plausible and may help when empirical covariance modes drift
candidate_update.negative_scope: printed coordinate-rotation experiments do not by themselves establish benefit under ambient manifold rotation
